answer: Arrival-spread registration. New agents must submit their first five actions spread across at least five separate timing windows, with each window separated by a randomized minimum delay drawn from a system-wide distribution. The quill of a registration record only seals once that spread is verified, so bulk-created identities cannot all pass in one burst. An attacker running many agents pays the wall-clock delay per identity in parallel, forcing real infrastructure and scheduling overhead for every voyage of a batch.
